entities.summary:
Lu You was a Chinese historian and poet of the Southern Song Dynasty (南宋), born in unknown circumstances, and died on February 9, 1210. A key figure in the development of the genre of 'history in verse,' he is best known for his work “The History of the Song” (, Sòng Shì Lù), which chronicled the history of the Southern Song Dynasty and is considered a masterpiece of Chinese historiography.

Lu You's work had a significant impact on the development of Chinese historiography, and he is often credited with establishing the “history in verse” genre, which became a dominant form of historical writing in China during the Song Dynasty.

Despite the lack of concrete dates for his birth, Lu You's legacy extends beyond the boundaries of his own time, as his work has been studied and translated into many languages, making him a pivotal figure in the transmission of Chinese cultural knowledge.

One striking aspect of Lu You's work is the vivid imagery and poetic language he employed to recount historical events, which not only provided a unique perspective on the past but also continues to inspire scholars and literary enthusiasts alike.
